speaker: freelancer
text: With esp32s3, i2c does not require the hardware-defined pins; any two pins can be used.

speaker: client
text: That is useful to know about the pins, but the current pins are already arranged and should work, unless you notice a problem with them.

speaker: freelancer
text: Because GPIO3 is a strapping boot pin, it isn't suitable for unrestricted use here.

speaker: client
text: That was my mistake: GPIO3 came from my original ESP32 design. Use GPIO5 for 5V_EN instead. I also realized that GPIO22, GPIO23, GPIO25, and GPIO27 are not exposed on the WROOM-1 module, so SCL0 must move from GPIO22 to GPIO38 and SPI MOSI from GPIO23 to GPIO26. I'll update the documentation and send you the complete revised GPIO table.

speaker: freelancer
text: The proposed SPI MOSI destination, GPIO26, is unavailable too.

speaker: freelancer
text: Am I correct that this board contains the esp32, ina219, usb, connectors, and their related components?

speaker: client
text:
Correct. Sensors and power-management circuitry stay on the other boards; the main board contains:

\- ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 module
\- INA219 current monitor measuring the 3.3V rail
\- USB-C programming connector plus an LDO for standalone operation
\- All JST connectors for the power board, sensor board, display, PIR, touch inputs, LEDs, buttons, and reset
\- Supporting components including decoupling capacitors, pull-ups, series resistors, Schottky diodes, and a BOOT button

speaker: client
text: A reset button and a switch are included as well, and I think there are 2 additional buttons.
